text:
ryan: Heads-up — after the hybrid-quant + new kernel routing rollout this morning I’m seeing a sharp drop in lead-in prefix hit rate for a subset of models. Not an overall regression but a consistent warmup collapse for 2/3 customer workloads.
ben: Which models / profiles? can you paste a short metric snapshot?
ryan: Observed on rwd-7b-v2 and community-ggml-7b-like. Quick snapshot from warmup-trace: 
```
cache_window: 120s
model: rwd-7b-v2
prefix_hit_rate: 0.87 -> 0.61
median_latency_ms: 48 -> 53
first_token_latency_ms: 16 -> 28
warmup_samples: 240 -> 58
```
carmen: That first_token latency jump + hit_rate dip screams key mismatch or affinity reshuffle. We changed kernel-selection affinity so small-seq traffic got moved to matmul-tiling variant yesterday. Also the hybrid quant toggle introduced a different kv-key canonicalization in the compiler path.
marie: I saw a similar shape in canary: short-lived warmup plateau then sudden decay at t+30s after model load. Looks like the batcher shortened lookahead, so fewer prefetches were surfaced.
ben: Any overlap with recent batching heuristic flag flips? I flipped "adaptive-batch-horizon" to 0.6 for that pool at 03:02 during canary.
ryan: Yes, that’s likely — routing + smaller horizon = missing the prefetch window. But the kv-key canonicalization change could cause salt mismatch: keys generated by matmul-tiling kernel differ when quant path takes a slightly different input padding order.
ben: Can you attach a tiny repro? sample inputs that hit the low-case path?
ryan: Dropping a minimal trace: 
```
> request id: s-8adf
> prompt: "Summarize the following document..."
> seq-len dist: [8,12,16,8,4,8]
> buildid: 202.44
> kernel_variant: mattiling-v2
> quant_profile: hybrid-q8
> generated_kv_key_prefix: 0x9f4a..d2 vs 0x9f4a..d3
```
carmen: That one-byte diff in key suffix explains the miss. Looks like the quant path changed pad-trailing-zero behavior; canonicalization used to strip trailing padding before hashing but new compile leaves trailing pad in small-batch codegen.
marie: Ops update — canary was promoted at 03:14 to 30% then 100% for that region. deploy-bot: rolled out build 202.44 -> deploy-id: d-202.44 (canary -> prod). :warning:
deploy-bot: rollback suggestion queued? Use `deploy rollback d-202.44` if we confirm cross-key drift.
ben: Immediate mitigations: 1) roll back to build 202.41 (old canonicalization) 2) force batcher horizon back to 0.9 for the affected pool 3) enable a temporary prefetch TTL bump to 300s 4) add a quick KV normalization shim in runtime to strip trailing padding before hash. Which do we want first?
ryan: Prioritize rollback + batcher horizon bump. KV shim as near-term patch if rollback not fast enough. Also want a small integration test to assert canonicalization parity between mattiling and matmul kernels.
carmen: I'll open a small PR for the normalization shim and a test that runs both codegen paths with deterministic inputs. Tagging @ben for deploy permissions.
marie: I’m going to temporarily throttle promotions for build 202.44 across regions and flip canary back to 30%. deploy-bot: set canary=30% for d-202.44 in us-west.
deploy-bot: canary updated -> 30% (us-west)
ben: I kicked the rollback; ops plan in #incidents if we need on-call. Also adding a perf regression eval to CI to check prefix hit-rate delta > 0.05 post-compile.
ryan: Thanks — will collect targeted traces for the test harness. If anyone sees other models with similar pattern please paste traces here. :thumbsup:
